prs.title: feat(git): land worktree changes into the base branch
prs.body:
You had to finish a worktree thread by hand: merge, remove the worktree, then delete the branch.

- "Land" commits any changes, merges the worktree branch into its base branch in the main checkout, then removes the worktree and deletes its branch.

- After a land, the thread moves to the main checkout on the base branch.
- Progress shows the new merge and cleanup steps.

prs.title: feat(git): sync branches before push and record git actions
prs.body:
A push or pull request from the Git controls could fail or open a stale PR when the remote branch or the default branch had moved. The agent also did not know about Git actions the user ran from the controls.

- Before a push or PR, the server fetches the remote. It rebases the branch onto its upstream and onto the default branch when either has new commits. A rebase that rewrites pushed commits pushes with `--force-with-lease`.
- **Land worktree** rebases onto the base branch in the worktree before it merges.
- If a rebase stops on conflicts, the rebase stays in progress. `askAgentToResolveRebase` queues a message that asks the thread's agent to finish it. The action fails, and its message says the agent is resolving it.
- Each Git action is recorded in the thread (`recordGitAction`, `GitActionNote`). The agent sees the actions at the start of its next turn.
- Generated commit and PR text reads the thread's conversation, so it can explain why the change was made.

Tests are in `GitManager.test.ts`, `GitActionNote.test.ts`, `Orchestrator.control-reads.test.ts`, and `textGenerationPrompts.test.ts`.

The base is `base/mine-a83e8fd`, the parent of this commit on `mine`. This work depends on #2, #3, and #4, and they could not be ported to an orchestration-v2 base without a rewrite.

prs.title: feat(web): collapse chat history into summaries
prs.body:
A long thread gets busy, and there was no way to tidy the history you have already read.

- **Collapse history** in the chat header menu folds everything since the previous collapse into one row. The row shows "Collapsed (summarizing)" at once.
- The server asks the text generation model for a one-line summary and replaces the placeholder with it. If that fails, the row shows "Collapsed".
- You can collapse many times. Each collapse covers only what came after the previous one.
- Click a row to look inside it for the current visit. Its **×** uncollapses it for good.
- Collapses are saved with the thread. They change only the display, not what the provider sees. An agent that reads the thread through MCP sees one line that marks the collapse and gives its summary.
- The server rejects a collapse while a turn runs or when nothing new needs collapsing.

How it works:

- A collapse is a runless `history_collapse` timeline item, stored like the git-action item, so there is no migration. Its status is `running` while it summarizes, `completed` after, and `cancelled` when you uncollapse it.
- New commands: `thread.history.collapse`, `thread.history.uncollapse`, and the internal `thread.history-collapse.complete`.
- `HistoryCollapseSummaryService` runs from a `history-collapse.summarize` effect. That effect shares the per-thread lane with title generation, so it never delays provider effects.
- `generateHistorySummary` is a new text generation operation for every provider, Muse included. ACP Registry and FX do not support it.
- Clients show the menu item only when the server reports the `threadHistoryCollapse` capability.
- The thread sidebar user guide describes the feature.

Not included: mobile shows a "Collapsed: summary" row but does not hide the history. There is no keybinding, command palette entry, or MCP tool, and find-in-thread does not open a collapse.

Tests are in `HistoryCollapse.test.ts` and `MessagesTimeline.logic.test.ts`. I did not check it in a running app.

The base is `base/mine-4869a6f`, the parent of this commit on `mine`.

prs.title: fix(git): land branches without requiring main checkout
prs.body:
Landing a worktree failed unless the main checkout was on the base branch: "The main checkout at … is on other. Switch it to main, then land again." You had to switch branches in a checkout you were not using.

Landing now finds the worktree that has the base branch checked out, if one does:

- **No checkout has the base branch.** Landing moves the base branch ref forward. No working tree changes.
- **A checkout has the base branch.** Landing updates that checkout, as before. It refuses if that checkout has uncommitted changes, and the error names its path.
- The main checkout keeps its current branch and stays clean.
- A rebase conflict stays in the worktree being landed, as before.
- When the main checkout is not on the base branch, the success toast does not offer to push. A push from there would push the wrong branch.

Tests in `GitManager.test.ts` cover these cases: landing while main is on another branch, updating a separate checkout of main, refusing when that checkout is dirty, and keeping a conflict in the worktree.

prs.title: fix(web): size ordered list gutters to fit markers
prs.body:
In the composer, ordered list markers such as `10. ` are drawn as source text. In a monospace font a marker can be wider than the default list gutter, so it hangs to the left of the text column. In chat messages, the default `1.25rem` gutter is also too narrow for `1. ` in a monospace chat font, so a collapsed message's overflow can clip the marker.

The default `ol` gutter for chat and the composer is now `3ch`. That width fits a one-digit marker, its period, and the trailing space in any font. ChatMarkdown still widens the gutter for lists with longer markers.

A small ProseMirror plugin sets `--list-gutter` on each composer ordered list to the width of its widest marker plus one space, in `ch`. It is a decoration and not `renderHTML`, because the list element is not redrawn when only its items change.

No before/after screenshots yet.

prs.title: feat(web): show item runtime in work logs
prs.body:
A row in the work log did not show how long its item ran. You had to compare timestamps to find a slow command or tool call.

- A completed work log row shows its runtime to the left of the disclosure chevron, for example `850ms`, `4.2s`, or `1m 3s`. It uses the same `formatDuration` as the rest of the app.
- The runtime comes from the item's `startedAt` and `completedAt`. Any item type with both values gets the label, not only commands.
- The hover timestamp still appears, to the left of the runtime, and the chevron does not move.
- Some rows show no runtime:
  - A running item. A live timer would redraw the row all the time.
  - An interrupted item. Cleanup closes it long after it stopped, so the duration is wrong.
  - A question or an approval request. Its duration is the wait for the user, not work.
  - An item that starts and completes at the same time.

prs.title: feat(web): show remote server health in thread details
prs.body:
When a remote server felt slow, there was no way to tell from the client if the cause was the network or the server.

The thread details card now has a **Server** section for threads on a remote environment. The section does not show at the essential density. It starts collapsed. The header shows a summary such as `42 ms · CPU 37% · Mem 61%`, colored by the worst value. The open or closed state is saved in local storage.

The expanded rows, and when each turns amber / red:

| Row | Shows | Amber / red |
|---|---|---|
| Latency | Round trip from the client to the server | 150 ms / 400 ms |
| CPU | Host CPU %, with core count | 70% / 90% |
| Load (1 min) | Host load average (not on Windows) | 1× / 2× cores |
| Memory | Used of total | 80% / 92% |
| Server busy | Event loop utilization of the T3 server | 50% / 80% |
| Server memory | RSS of the T3 server | none |

How it works:

- No new RPC. `HostResourcesSnapshot` gets three optional fields: `loadAverage1m`, `eventLoopUtilization`, and `serverRssBytes`. A client still decodes snapshots from older servers, and it leaves out the rows for missing fields.
- `HostResources` slept 200 ms on every read to measure CPU, so a timed request measured that sleep and not the network. It now uses the previous sample as the first reading when that sample is less than 30 seconds old. CPU and event loop use become averages over the poll interval. `useLoadBalancedEnvironment` reads the same snapshot, so it gets that average too.
- A new `hostHealth` query in `client-runtime` polls every 10 seconds while the section is mounted and times each request for latency.
- The second commit stops the summary from widening the card. The card's scroll area sizes to its content, so the summary now has zero width, grows into the free space, and truncates.

Not included: mobile. On a macOS host, each poll still starts `vm_stat`, which adds a few milliseconds to latency. No server test for the sampler change.

No before/after screenshots yet.

The base is `base/mine-16579e2`, the parent of the first commit on `mine`.

prs.title: fix(server): place runless items after thread history
prs.body:
On a remote server, **Collapse history** added a "Collapsed" row at the top of the thread. It hid nothing and never got a summary.

`TurnItemPositionStore` puts each turn item's ordinal in its run's range, run ordinal × 1,000,000. A runless item has no run, so it went into range 0 and sorted before every turn. On dds-dev the marker got ordinal 1, and the thread's turns used 1,000,001 to 3,000,011. The timeline hides what comes before a marker, and nothing did. The summary uses the same messages, so it was empty.

A runless item now goes into the range of the thread's latest run, after everything already in the thread. Git action rows are also runless, so this fix moves them to the correct place as well. An item with a run, or with a run ordinal from the same event batch, keeps its old placement.

This was not caught because `HistoryCollapse.test.ts` applies items straight to the projection and skips position allocation. The new `TurnItemPositionStore.test.ts` allocates positions before and after a run, and it fails without this fix.

A marker that already has a wrong ordinal keeps it. Uncollapse that marker, then collapse again.

The base is `base/mine-9a51b59`, the parent of this commit on `mine`.

prs.title: fix(web): make the activity shimmer easier to see
prs.body:
In some themes, the base color of the live activity label is already close to the foreground color. The shimmer sweep then barely changes the label, so it is hard to see.

prs.title: feat(web): show timestamps and context usage in minimap previews
prs.body:
The timeline minimap preview showed only the message text. You could not see when a turn happened or how full the context window was at that point.

The preview now has a footer with two details:

- The time the user message was sent, in the user's timestamp format, plus its age, such as "3 minutes ago" or "4 weeks ago".
- The context usage that the turn's run ended with, as a percentage and token count, such as "Context 12% · 120k/1M". If the provider does not report a maximum, only the token count shows. If the run has no usage report, the line does not show.

`tokenUsageByRunId` in `lib/contextWindow.ts` maps each run to the newest token usage report across its attempts' provider turns. `ChatView` computes this map and passes it through `MessagesTimeline` to `TimelineMinimap`. `formatApproximateAge` in `timestampFormat.ts` makes the age text. Both functions have tests.

prs.head: 86aa6c77cc3211f09e2f3f57c5020c2b199f6e97

prs.title: feat(web): pin the current prompt in the timeline
prs.body:
In a long turn, the prompt scrolls out of view. You then lose track of which request the agent's output answers.

When a prompt scrolls fully above the viewport, a compact copy of it now stays pinned at the top of the timeline. The copy shows at most two lines. Click it to scroll back to the prompt. As the next prompt reaches the top, it pushes the pinned copy up and then takes its place. The scroll handler sets this offset directly on the DOM, so scrolling does not re-render the timeline on each frame. The pinned prompt is hidden while find is open.

The pin is on by default. A "Pin current prompt" switch in the thread details panel turns it off for one thread. Opt-outs persist in local storage. The switch does not show for drafts or in the essential density.

`resolveTimelinePinnedPrompt` picks the pinned prompt from the list layout, and focused tests cover it.
